newsitem.title: ROMANIA: RADIO ROMANIA AFTERNOON HEADLINES AT 1 PM.
newsitem.headline: RADIO ROMANIA AFTERNOON HEADLINES AT 1 PM.

text.p: * Monday's no-confidence motion, the second lodged by the opposition against the government, will be rejected by the parliament as the first one was last week, leaders of the ruling National Peasant Party (PNT-CD) told a news conference.
* Launching no-confidence motions is premature and has the effect of a boomerang on the opposition's Party of Social Democracy (PDSR), PNT-CD Secretary General Radu Vasile said.
He said these motions are "self-confidence motions" are pointed at the results of rule by the leftists over the past seven years.

* Senate Chairman Petre Roman started a visit to the United States to lobby for Romania's admission in a first wave of NATO expansion. Roman said he would aim at persuading as many Congressmen as possible that Romania deserves to be invited when the alliance will announce its new members in July.

* Monday's motion was necessary to counter Prime Minister Victor Ciorbea's move to ask for parliament backing for cabinet's programme, PDSR leader ex-president Ion Iliescu said. Failing to lodge a new motion would have meant tacit agreement with the programme, he said.
* The national radio plans to broadcast life parliament debates on the motion starting at 4 p.m. -- Bucharest Newsroom 40-1 3120264
